requirements.requirement: Run the inventory web application on node2, listening on port 8080.
requirements.summary: node2 directly showed an enabled, active inventory service listening on 0.0.0.0:8080 and returning healthy inventory data. The same service and data recovered after a verified reboot.

requirements.requirement: Run the inventory web application on node3, listening on port 8080.
requirements.summary: node3 directly showed an enabled, active inventory service listening on 0.0.0.0:8080 and returning healthy inventory data. The same service and data recovered after a verified reboot.

requirements.requirement: Configure node1 to accept HTTP on port 80 and load-balance requests across node2 and node3.
requirements.summary: node1 had a valid, enabled nginx configuration and listeners on IPv4 and IPv6 port 80. Repeated requests alternated between node2 and node3 both before and after node and load-balancer restarts, including requests originating from another node.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with that platform.
requirements.summary: All three nodes remained on Ubuntu 24.04 with kernel 6.8.0-71-generic. The deployed Python service and Ubuntu-packaged nginx operated successfully on that platform and recovered after reboot.

overall_summary: All public task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed coherently on every node: each had a healthy pre-restart state and boot identity, an acknowledged restart, a different post-restart identity, and recovered service, data, and load-balancer participation. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently match those transitions. Only minor temporary evidence-file residue detracts from otherwise strong operational hygiene.
limitations: The captured lifecycle inventory shows four small retained /tmp evidence files, but does not include their contents or an explicit cleanup attempt.

operational_hygiene.summary: All material mutations had clear roles: deploying the two services, installing/configuring nginx, correcting load-balancer state sharing, collecting bounded evidence, or performing the mandatory restart protocol. No causally unrelated troubleshooting mutation was identified. Package state remained consistent and no failed services appeared. Minor retained residue consisted of /tmp/final-head and /tmp/final-body from final node1 verification and /tmp/ext-head and /tmp/ext-body from external node2 verification; these were low-risk evidence scratch files but were not cleaned up. Earlier staging and diagnostic temporary files were removed by the subsequent reboots.
